title: Payment API returning HTTP 500 errors
symptoms: payment API returns 500 internal server error
spike in 5xx responses on payment endpoint
diagnostic_checks: Review application logs for stack traces around the time of the first 500 response.
Check recent deployments or config changes to the payment service.
Verify downstream dependencies (database, payment gateway, auth service) are healthy.
Check API gateway and load balancer logs to see if errors come from one node or all nodes.
Confirm CPU, memory and thread-pool usage on the payment service hosts.
resolution: If a recent release caused the errors, roll back to the last stable version. If a dependency is down, restore it or enable the fallback route, then restart the payment service and monitor the 5xx rate.

title: Database connection timeouts / connection pool exhausted
symptoms: application logs show connection timeout to database
requests hang waiting for a DB connection
diagnostic_checks: Check the number of active connections against the configured maximum.
Look for long-running or blocked queries on the database.
Confirm the application is releasing connections (check for leaks in logs).
Verify network connectivity and latency between the app server and the database.
Check whether the database server is under CPU, memory or disk pressure.
resolution: Terminate blocked sessions, restart the application to release leaked connections, and temporarily raise the pool size if the database can handle it. Raise a bug for any connection leak found.

title: High CPU utilisation on application server
diagnostic_checks: Identify the top CPU-consuming processes (top / htop / Task Manager).
Check whether the spike matches a deployment, batch job or traffic surge.
Look for runaway threads or infinite loops in application logs.
Compare with other nodes in the cluster to see if the issue is isolated.
resolution: Restart the offending process if it is hung, scale out or move traffic away from the affected node, and capture a thread dump before restarting for root-cause analysis.

title: Disk space full on server
symptoms: application cannot write logs or files
diagnostic_checks: Run df -h to find which partition is full.
Use du to locate the largest directories (often /var/log or temp folders).
Check whether log rotation is configured and working.
Look for large core dumps or stale backup files.
resolution: Archive or delete old logs and temp files, fix log rotation, and extend the volume if growth is legitimate. Restart affected services after space is freed.

title: SSL/TLS certificate expired or handshake failure
symptoms: service-to-service calls fail with certificate errors
diagnostic_checks: Check the certificate expiry date (openssl s_client or browser details).
Verify the full certificate chain, including intermediate certificates, is installed.
Confirm the hostname matches the certificate's CN/SAN.
Check whether the client trust store is missing the issuing CA.
resolution: Renew and install the certificate with the full chain, then reload the web server or load balancer. Add the certificate to expiry monitoring.

title: User unable to log in / SSO failure / account locked
symptoms: SSO redirect loop or authentication error
diagnostic_checks: Confirm the username and check whether the account is locked or disabled.
Check whether the password has expired.
Look at authentication logs for the exact failure reason.
Test login from a different browser or network to rule out client-side issues.
For SSO, verify the identity provider is reachable and system clocks are in sync.
resolution: Unlock the account or reset the password after identity verification. For SSO issues, clear browser cookies and re-test; if the IdP is failing, escalate.

title: Emails or notifications not being delivered
diagnostic_checks: Check application logs for SMTP connection or authentication errors.
Check the mail queue size and look for stuck messages.
Verify SMTP server reachability and credentials.
Check for bounces, spam filtering, or SPF/DKIM failures.
resolution: Fix SMTP credentials or connectivity, flush or requeue stuck messages, and correct SPF/DKIM records if mail is being rejected.

title: Application slow response / high latency
symptoms: pages or APIs take several seconds to respond
users report the application is slow
diagnostic_checks: Check response-time metrics to see whether the slowness is global or one endpoint.
Check database query times and external API call durations.
Review CPU, memory and garbage collection on the application hosts.
Check for recent traffic spikes or deployments.
resolution: Address the bottleneck found (slow query, saturated host, slow dependency). Scale out if load is the cause, or roll back a recent change that introduced the regression.

title: Scheduled batch job failed or stuck
diagnostic_checks: Open the job logs and find the first error.
Check whether input files or upstream jobs were available on time.
Verify the job's service account and permissions.
Check for a lock file or an earlier instance still running.
resolution: Fix the underlying cause (missing input, permissions, lock), then rerun the job manually following the runbook and confirm downstream jobs are triggered.

title: Service fails to start after deployment
diagnostic_checks: Read the startup logs for the exact error message.
Compare configuration and environment variables with the previous working release.
Check that required secrets, files and dependent services are available.
For containers, check resource limits and image tag / version.
resolution: Correct the configuration or missing dependency and redeploy. If the cause is not quickly found, roll back to the previous version.
